newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi streamlines cabinet, four ministries axed.
newsitem.headline: Malawi streamlines cabinet, four ministries axed.

text.p: The Malawi government announced on Saturday that it had dissolved its cabinet in order to form a smaller one.
Secretary in the president's office Alfred Upindi told reporters the size of the cabinet would be reduced from 26 ministries to 22 as part of the government's civil service reform programme.

"The cabinet committee on civil service reform has now completed its task of examining the recommendations ... and the government has approved a new structure of the government of Malawi," Upindi said.
He said four ministries had been eliminated while others would be merged.
Upindi declined to say when President Bakili Muluzi would announce a new cabinet. "Normally it should not be too long."
The restructuring exercise will continue with an evaluation of every job in the civil service and is expected to be completed by November 1998.
"If there are excess bodies I'll recommend that they retire," Upindi said.
Ministries that will be axed are Natural Resources, Research and Environmental Affairs, Youth, Sports and Culture and Economic Planning and Development.

The Irrigation and Water Development ministries will be merged to form the Water Ministry; the Relief and Rehabilitation Ministry will be merged into the office of president; while the three Housing, Land and Physical Planning ministries will also be merged.
